description:
We are a passionate team of Computer Engineering students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We're developing LEGACY, an interactive educational space exploration game that combines real NASA science, astronaut experiences, and exciting missions.

Our team brings skills in software development, problem-solving, and creative thinking. We're looking for enthusiastic teammates with interests in game development, 3D design, UI/UX, and space science.
summary: LEGACY is a 3D browser game, in English and Arabic, in which students aged 13–18 become mission commanders. It answers the Space Mission Design Game challenge by turning real engineering trade-offs into play. There are four missions: a crewed Apollo-heritage expedition to the Moon, a robotic search for a potential biosignature in Jezero Crater, a mission to document NASA's Opportunity rover, and a space telescope racing to catch a supernova. In each one, players design a spacecraft within a fixed budget and mass, power, data and thermal limits. A readiness review explains every failure. Players then launch and operate on another world. Choices made on Earth carry through: battery size limits how far a rover can drive, the instruments decide which evidence can be collected, and the antenna decides how much data reaches Earth. A What-If Machine re-runs the mission with a different design and shows the recomputed result. Built on NASA imagery, mission records and the challenge's own NASA resources, LEGACY teaches that good missions balance science, engineering and safety, and that evidence comes before certainty.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: LEGACY is a story-driven mission design game that runs in any browser. The player chooses one of four missions and answers a 3-question baseline check. They pick a science question, then build a rover, lander or telescope within a fixed budget. Every part changes cost, mass, power, data and heat together. Live checks are grouped into NASA's four mission segments (Launch, Space, Ground, User), and a Concept Maturity line shows the design moving from concept to point design. Launch is blocked until every mandatory requirement passes, and the game explains exactly why. After a cinematic launch, players explore freely: drive a six-wheel rover across Mars, ride the lunar rover on the Moon, manage crew health inside the spacecraft cabin, or operate a telescope over several nights. Events such as dust storms, solar flares and crew fatigue force decisions, and the game then explains which choice was best and why. A report is scored on honesty: a "potential biosignature" is not proof of life. A What-If Machine replays the mission with a different design and recomputes the outcome. A short final quiz helps assess changes in the player's understanding.

HOW IT WORKS: A deterministic TypeScript simulation records every decision as an action, so saves, rewind and What-If replay the same rules. The 3D world is rendered with Three.js and React Three Fiber. Everything is fully translated into Arabic, with right-to-left layout.

NASA DATA: Players choose a landing site on NASA's Jezero Crater image. Each instrument returns real Perseverance data: the Cheyava Falls image, the PIXL mineral map and the Sapphire Canyon core. Protected zones at the Apollo 15 and Opportunity sites follow NASA's recommendations for protecting lunar historic sites. Crew health follows the NASA Human Research Program's spaceflight hazards. The workshop applies NASA's "Design and Develop Science Missions" and JPL's Concept Maturity Levels from the challenge resources. Every number is labelled as a NASA fact, a calculation or a game value.

IMPACT: LEGACY addresses the gap between learning about space missions and understanding the engineering decisions behind them. It gives students aged 13–18 a hands-on way to experiment with limited resources, experience consequences, and learn from mistakes. Its What-If Machine encourages critical thinking by letting students compare alternative decisions. English and Arabic support make the experience accessible to a wider audience. Built-in before-and-after questions offer an initial way to assess understanding, while further student testing is needed to measure learning impact.

CREATIVITY: One rule system covers crewed, robotic, heritage and astronomy missions. Earth choices echo through a free-roaming 3D world. Outcomes are actually recomputed, not prewritten. Historic sites have narrated stories.

TOOLS: TypeScript, React, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Zustand, Vite, Vitest, Playwright, Web Audio, and Google Gemini text-to-speech. Hosted on Vercel. Source code: https://github.com/awshammad04/LEGACY

FACTORS CONSIDERED: Scientific accuracy labels, accessibility (keyboard and touch controls, subtitles, reduced motion), Arabic right-to-left layout, low bandwidth, ethics (heritage protection; crew health values are simulated), and no NASA branding.
